We have search results with two templates. Template 3196 has mapped_rxn string. Need to return mapped_rxn and template_id as integer. The task: "return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule below, reproduces the reaction: ... SN2 ... halide broken, new C-N formed." We need to find template that matches SN2. The search gave template 3196 (retro_smarts: [#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]1...>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])-[c:3]...). That seems not SN2 but maybe amide formation? Actually looks like conversion of amide to something else. The other template 1321 is similar.

But we need SN2: halide broken, amine formed. The molecule is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. It contains a side chain with CN4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine). SN2 would involve a halide leaving group, but the molecule doesn't have halide. However maybe retrosynthetic step: break C-N bond to generate halide? The template likely breaks C-N to form halide (reverse SN2). So we need template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse) breaks C-N and forms halide. The search criteria we used: broken halide, formed amines. That gave templates that match. Which one is appropriate? Need to check if template matches the molecule. We already checked template 3196 matches (True). Also template 1321 likely matches too. Let's check 1321.
